assets.statement: L1-as-branch-B-evidence fails: Maynard bound is subsequence-only (hidden-subsequence attack) and does not match the quantifier reversal of o(log N) (needs all-N failure at positive density, not infinitely many N); repair = uniform c·log N lower bound on the full primes, an equivalent-strength open p

REFUTED by external audit (GPT gold-mine audit + R4, 2026-09-01), each item re-verified by the operator's session against the frozen contract or by exact computation on 2026-09-02 | FALSE: Pintz/Rankin-type results concern LARGE GAPS between consecutive primes, not the length of arithmetic progressions of primes in [1,N]. No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.
Literal statement false: cofinite B makes A∖B finite, so no (k+1)-basis; repair = require A∖B infinite, after which the problem is a genuine open question with no counterexample found.

counterexample n=11: 11=2^3+3 in the stated exclusion family yet 11=7+2^1+2^1 with prime 7, so sufficiency of the 2^l+3 family fails; repair requires a three-stratum covering bound with proved density transfer, both open

[REFUTED-BY-ADVERSARIAL-MINE-2026-09-02: opus ranked-claims auditor, exact computation/derivation, receipt scratchpad/mine/agent-ranked.jsonl] Hindman gives FS(B), sums of DISTINCT elements; A+A also contains a+a=2a, which FS omits. That gap is exactly why the problem is open, so this is not an affirmative close. The alt row concedes it.

Counterexample A=ℝ: every affine image is ℝ, not meager, so the meagerness lemma and its fat-Cantor proof route fail; a correct affirmative close needs a different construction uniform in all infinite A.
